note_tweet.text:
For 300 consecutive days, I woke up at 5:00 AM to memorize English vocabulary and ancient Chinese poetry.
→ This is basically the entire final year of high school with almost zero rest days.
My normal routine in senior year was:
Breakfast: 3 minutes
Lunch: 10 minutes
Dinner: 9 minutes
→ Students often eat standing up or while reviewing notes. Total eating time per day can be under 25 minutes.
To increase my speed on the Science Comprehensive paper, I once completed 6 full sets of practice exams in a single day.
→ Each set is a full 3-hour Gaokao simulation. This is extreme even by Chinese standards.
I wrote out the past 15 years of real Gaokao exam questions 3 times.
→ Thousands of questions, done by hand. Many students do this multiple times.
To stay energetic, I sometimes drank 2 bags of extra-strong concentrated coffee in one day.
→ These are powerful “study aid” drinks sold specifically to exhausted Chinese students. Many develop heart issues or caffeine addiction.
To memorize every biology knowledge point, I read the entire biology textbook aloud from beginning to end 21 times, word for word.
→ This level of rote memorization is common. Chinese students are trained to recall information instantly under extreme time pressure.
My hands got rubbed raw from writing so many papers. I patched them with band-aids and kept doing math real questions.
→ Physical injury from writing is very common. Some students get calluses or even permanent scars.
I memorized 35 model Chinese essays almost word for word.
→ Essay memorization is a standard strategy for the Chinese composition section.
While others were taking afternoon naps or resting on weekends, I often stayed alone in the classroom grinding practice questions just to stay more focused.
→ Many schools have “self-study” sessions until 10–11 PM. Sleep is often 5–6 hours or less.
Every single day during my senior year, I crazily memorized 200 new English words. In the end, I raised my weak-subject English score from around 60 points to over 120 points.
→ This kind of daily grind turns many students into English memorization machines.
